title: Resume vs Job Description: How to Find the Skills You're Missing
subtitle: How to perform an instant skills gap analysis on any vacancy — and how to position transferable proficiencies for requirements you don't fully meet.
excerpt: Think you are qualified for a role, but the ATS says no? Discover how to run a forensic skills gap analysis between your CV and any job posting, and learn how to address missing requirements honestly.
featuredImageAlt: Comparative skills gap analysis matrix between candidate resume and job requirements
author: Amarjot Lohia

sections.heading: The Hidden Keyword Gap: Why You Feel Qualified When the ATS Disagrees
sections.content:
One of the most frustrating experiences in job hunting is reviewing a job description, feeling 100% confident in your ability to perform the role, and receiving an automated rejection email within 20 minutes.

This happens because of the lexical gap: you have the underlying capability, but your resume describes it using different terminology than what the ATS parser is configured to reward. If the posting requests 'Cross-functional stakeholder management' and your CV says 'Worked with diverse teams', the algorithm fails to register a match.

sections.heading: Categorizing the Discrepancy: Hard Skills vs Tools vs Methodologies
sections.content:
When analyzing a job posting against your Master CV, categorize missing terms into three buckets:

Bucket 1: Direct Matches (Keep & Highlight)

Technologies and skills you have executed directly. Ensure these appear in both your Skills list and accomplishment bullets.

Bucket 2: Semantic Equivalents (Re-label)

Capabilities you have practiced under a different industry term. Update your resume's phrasing to match the employer's specific vocabulary.

Bucket 3: Genuine Skill Gaps (Bridge with Adjacencies)

Tools or frameworks you have not used yet. Bridge the gap by demonstrating adjacent mastery (e.g., highlighting deep PostgreSQL expertise when the job mentions MySQL).

faqs.question: What should I do if I am missing 30% of the listed requirements?
faqs.answer: If the missing 30% consists of secondary tools or 'nice-to-haves', apply! Focus your cover letter and summary on your rapid ramp-up track record and mastery of core foundational principles.
